items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: when I listen to Miles Davis and Wayne Shorter

ctx.x: Did your combining of these certain elements, do you run into let’s say problem solving situations with scales that might be inherently Chinese and our music here, based on diatonic scales, etc. How do you work those together?

Well one of the questions I asked is the tuning, western and non-western tuning. And I kind of equate my experience when I used to perform in the joints — I didn’t perform in the blues clubs like in Oakland, and that was probably a learning lesson for me both in terms of music, and trying to respect the music, and also socially. Because it’s just very atypical for a Chinese-American to be performing in the joints in Oakland, in an African- American club. But when you have like a singer who is bending the pitch,…
